A very interesting video bringing up the uncertainty about the climate science, but I think he makes far too broad generalisations and assumptions about the science itself when, if you listen to his points, his problem really lies with the reporting about the science. Science is never 'settled', as he claims that the climate science supposedly proclaims. Science strives to give a more accurate description about our universe; anyone claiming any science is 'settled' is in effect not using a scientific approach.

Example: It is settled that Newtonian physics are correct... with the caveat that we are talking about here on earth and that we are not talking about quantum physics since Newton's laws break down in singularities. This doesn't mean that we should find a workaround to explain how Newton's laws do work in singularities to preserve that explanation model - but it also doesn't mean that Newton's laws are irrelevant.

Much in the same way, it is settled that global temperatures have increased since the industrial revolution... with the caveat that they have flattened during the recent 18 years. This does not mean that we must come up with explanations within our current climate models - but it also doesn't mean we should reject the models altogether.

The problem with trying to explain away the pause is that we didn't see it coming, so these explanations are starting from the premise that global warming is occurring, and then fudging the endless available data into statistics that prove the researcher's existing beliefs. Until the scientists can predict these changes with a prospective model, all this shows is how little we really understand climate science.
